text.arabic_uthmani: تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ ٱلْمَضَاجِعِ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ خَوْفًۭا وَطَمَعًۭا وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَٰهُمْ يُنفِقُونَ

baseline.text: Yanları yataklardan uzaklaşır; Rablerine korku ve umutla yalvarırlar, kendilerine verdiğimiz şeylerden harcarlar.

findings.text: Bedenin yatakla temasını kesmesi, bir yakınlıktan ayrılarak Rabbe seslenme yakınlığına yönelen bilinçli bir mekân değişimidir.
Korku zarardan uzaklaştırırken umut Rabbe doğru çeker; iki yönlü etki, yakarışı yalnız paniğe ya da isteğe indirgenmekten korur.
Verilenlerin dışarı çıkışı, alan kişiyi nimetin son deposu değil, başkalarına ulaştığı bir geçit gibi düşündürür; ileride ateşten çıkışın kapanması bu çağrışımı tersinden güçlendirir.

activation_trace.role: Non-adherence supplies the active separation that governs the posture.
The bodily side supplies the moving surface rather than an abstract self.
Lateral adhesion to the ground supplies the resting relation being reversed.

changed_reading.after: Their worship begins as a repeated bodily unfastening: the very side fitted to cling to a resting surface creates distance from it.
changed_reading.before: They get out of bed to worship.

baseline_models.mechanism: The clause reverses a precise body-surface relation: the side, whose resting posture is adhesion to a lateral surface, repeatedly refuses that adhesion and makes distance.

activation_trace.role: Vocal calling that inclines toward an addressee supplies the central directed act.
Progressive nurture and completion make the addressee the one toward whom need is directed.
Anticipation of harm supplies the repelling vector.
The heart's expectant desire supplies the attracting vector.

changed_reading.after: Their call holds an unresolved push-pull field: feared harm drives them away while hoped-for nurture draws them toward the same Lord.
changed_reading.before: They pray with two named emotions, fear and hope.

baseline_models.mechanism: Calling is a speech-act of inclination toward the sustaining Lord while fear repels from anticipated harm and hope attracts toward desired good; the prayer is generated inside both vectors, not after either is resolved.

activation_trace.role: An apportioned grant supplies the incoming share.
The going-out of wealth supplies the explicit outward transfer.
A passage with an outlet recasts the giver as conduit rather than endpoint.

changed_reading.after: What reaches them as an allotted gift remains provision by passing outward through them; reception creates a channel, not a stopping place.
changed_reading.before: They donate part of what they own.

baseline_models.mechanism: An apportioned arrival is deliberately made to leave, and the outlet branch of expenditure turns the recipients into a route through which provision continues rather than its terminal owners.

activation_trace.role: Abandoning or slackening in an affair supplies an ethical second layer to the bed.
Breaking adhesion supplies the transition out of that inaction.
Directed speech supplies the first resumed action.
Outgoing wealth supplies the second resumed action and makes the return to duty material.

changed_reading.after: The physical rising also images recovery from neglected charge: inertia is broken and responsibility resumes in both address and expenditure.
changed_reading.before: The verse praises loss of sleep followed by prayer and charity.

baseline_models.mechanism: The bed can carry the branch of lying down on an undertaking; withdrawal then becomes refusal of neglected responsibility, immediately realized in a verbal act and a material act.

activation_trace.role: Delivery downward supplies the incoming leg of the circulation.
Ordering an affair by its outcome supplies continuity across the circuit.
Ascent supplies the returning leg rather than a one-way descent.
The apportioned gift is the focus-level arrival entering the circuit.
The open passage makes the recipient a relay within that circuit.

changed_reading.after: Night prayer and expenditure answer an already moving order: received good is not arrested at the self but relayed into a larger descent-and-return circulation.
changed_reading.before: Provision arrives and believers independently give some away.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier descent, managed consequence, and ascent turn the focus provision-passage model into a circulation: what is delivered downward is answered by a body that disengages and by provision routed onward rather than arrested.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies descent, consequence-aware ordering, ascent, receipt, and an outlet; I infer one circulation joining them. A live alternative keeps cosmic administration and personal giving as parallel but separate motions.
structural_cues: 32:2 introduces delivery; 32:5 explicitly sequences heaven-to-earth movement and return; 32:16 couples receipt with outflow.

activation_trace.role: The lowered head supplies an involuntary terminal posture of shame.
A sudden falling motion supplies the voluntary transition into worship.
Deliberate lowliness supplies the chosen downward posture.
Non-adhesion supplies the contrasting chosen movement away from comfort.
Grounded lateral adhesion identifies the posture they refuse to prolong.

changed_reading.after: Piety governs bodily yield: they willingly go low before the signs, refuse low adhesion to comfort, and thereby differ from those lowered without agency.
changed_reading.before: Piety is pictured as rising upward out of bed.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context supplies forced head inversion, responsive falling in prostration, and then withdrawal of the sides from beds. The focus movement is therefore not generic upwardness; it belongs to a choreography in which moral agency appears in what the body willingly lowers before and what it refuses to remain attached to.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies three body orientations; I assign agency and object as the contrastive arrow. They may instead be only separate scenes of judgment, prostration, and night vigil.
structural_cues: The ordered posture sequence is inverted heads in 32:12, falling prostrate in 32:15, then sides separating from beds in 32:16.

activation_trace.role: Separation supplies the relinquishment of present settlement.
Bodily adhesion identifies the visible repose being relinquished.
Concealment keeps the alternative repose unavailable to present sight.
Settling and quieting of the eye supplies the replacement repose.
The seeing eye relocates rest from the body's side to perception.
Reciprocal recompense supplies the exchange relation between the two forms of rest.

changed_reading.after: They relinquish one kind of settling for another: visible bodily adhesion now is exchanged for a hidden settling of perception later.
changed_reading.before: They sacrifice sleep because they hope for an unspecified reward.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next ayah answers the rejected visible resting place with a hidden settling of the eyes awarded in return. The focus is not hostility to repose but an exchange between immediately available bodily settlement and concealed perceptual settlement.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacency, present detachment, hidden eye-settling, and recompense; I infer substitution between two reposes. The live alternative is a simpler sacrifice-then-reward sequence without material symmetry.
structural_cues: 32:17 immediately follows the focus and shifts from sides and beds to hidden eye-settling as recompense for action.

activation_trace.role: Successful separation supplies a present bodily exit.
A route with an outlet supplies a present material exit.
Joining a shelter supplies the favorable terminal abode.
Prepared hospitality makes that abode a receiving destination.
Joining a shelter also supplies the adverse terminal enclosure.
Penetration to the outside supplies the attempted escape.
Return after departure blocks the escape by restoring enclosure.

changed_reading.after: Both acts exercise the present capacity for release: body and provision can still pass outward, unlike the later enclosure from which attempted exit only produces forced return.
changed_reading.before: Leaving bed and spending are two meritorious acts.

context_deltas.mechanism: The paired future abodes sharpen two focus exits: sides successfully leave a bed and provision successfully leaves through an outlet, while those in the adverse abode repeatedly attempt to leave and are returned. Present detachability becomes morally urgent agency.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies present focus exits and a later exit-return trap; I read the bed as a micro-abode and current detachment as rehearsal. The alternative is that the focus vigil and future abodes share no operative spatial analogy.
structural_cues: 32:19 and 32:20 parallel two abodes, but 32:20 repeats an attempted exit followed by forced return.

activation_trace.role: Active non-attachment supplies the focus instance of turning away.
The bodily side makes withdrawal materially visible.
A reminder supplies the claim from which the wrongdoer withdraws.
Turning one's side away supplies the culpable mirror of the focus movement.
The same side-turning becomes commanded when directed away from persistent rejecters.

changed_reading.after: The ayah trains selective attachment: leave the bed, never leave the signs, and recognize that even turning away can be commanded when its object changes.
changed_reading.before: Separation from attachment is itself the pious movement.

context_deltas.mechanism: Around the focus, bodily turning-away is repeated with different objects: responsive people detach from beds, the wrongdoer turns a side away from remembered signs, and the messenger is told to turn from the rejecters. Withdrawal is not intrinsically virtuous; fidelity lies in selecting the right attachment and refusal.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies shared spatial grammar, side semantics, and three objects; I infer deliberate moral discrimination by object. The live alternative treats the recurrence as ordinary idiom without a designed contrast.
structural_cues: The focus, 32:22, and 32:30 each construct withdrawal with عَنْ, while changing its object from beds to signs to rejecters.

activation_trace.role: Rain as provision links the focus gift to the later water circuit.
A passage with an outlet supplies the transmission structure.
Driving a flow supplies directed delivery rather than accidental diffusion.
Land stripped of vegetation supplies the receiving site of lack.
Bringing something out of concealment supplies transformed re-emergence.
Cultivated growth supplies the productive effect of the delivered resource.
An edible apportioned share completes the flow as renewed provision.

changed_reading.after: Spending routes provision into barrenness so that it can re-emerge as another's share; apparent loss at the source is one stage of growth.
changed_reading.before: Spending diminishes a received stock for another's benefit.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later water sequence gives the focus provision-passage a material analogue: directed supply enters plantless ground, emerges as growth, and becomes an edible share. Expenditure can therefore be read as generative redistribution into a site of lack, not simple subtraction from the giver.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies rain-provision, an outlet, and the later water-to-food chain; I infer social expenditure follows the same generative hydraulics. The alternative leaves the agricultural sign and human giving as separate examples of provision.
structural_cues: 32:27 orders a material chain: water is driven to barren land, growth is brought out, and creatures consume it.

remaining_uncertainties: The vertical circulation may be thematic parallelism rather than one causal circuit.
The bed-as-micro-abode and hydraulic-clearance readings depend on explicit but distant material analogies.
The د ع ع recovery activation is licensed by the split inventory but should remain subordinate to ordinary calling.
strongest_changes: The posture sequence replaces a simple upward piety with deliberate control over when the body descends and what it leaves.
The immediate hidden eye-settling turns rejected sleep into an exchange between visible and concealed repose.
Repeated turning-away constructions make detachment morally selective rather than inherently good.
The later water-to-food chain transforms expenditure from depletion into generative redistribution.
summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah behaves as a compact hinge: side, bed, call, affect, provision, and outlet preserve several simultaneous geometries of posture, attraction, circulation, selective refusal, and growth without requiring one final reading.

activation_trace.role: Ordinary directed calling preserves the surface action of the focus verb.
The encouragement to a stumbler to rise or recover makes the call echo the body's own recovery from recumbency.
Physical non-adhesion gives the recovery echo a visible focus anchor.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the call also reverberates as a recovery-command: in calling, the recumbent self enacts 'rise and recover' as well as addressing the Lord.
changed_reading.before: After rising, they direct prayer to their Lord.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the non-dominant د ع ع mapping behind the focus form rather than the ordinary call branch. It remains anchored to word 5 and coheres with the body's release from the bed, but downstream prose should present it only as a secondary phonetic-morphological activation, not as the lexical gloss of يَدْعُونَ.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: يَدْعُونَ within the bodily movement away from the beds

activation_trace.role: Residue cast to the side by a current supplies a clearing rather than merely rising image.
Rain-like provision supplies the moving medium.
A through-passage supplies continued flow instead of accumulation.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Physical separation enabling relational nearness.** **ج ف و B001** supplies standing away from contact, **ج ن ب B001** the bodily flank, **ض ج ع B001** the lying-place, and **د ع و B001** calling in order to draw near. The body moves away from one contact while the voice seeks another proximity. I infer that detachment from the bed creates the interval in which calling can operate. Their wakefulness reads as spatial reorientation, not mere sleep deprivation.
2. **Action held between fear and desire.** **خ و ف B001** supplies anticipation of harm, **ط م ع B001** heartfelt hope, **ر ز ق B001** allotted provision, and **ن ف ق B002** wealth going out as expenditure. The paired accusatives bracket prayer, and expenditure follows received provision. I infer that fear prevents complacency while hope prevents paralysis; together they keep granted resources moving outward. Devotion reads as a regulated flow rather than a single affect.
3. **Provision passing through an outlet (exploratory).** **ن ف ق B003** supplies a tunnel with an exit, a concrete image dormant beneath يُنفِقُونَ; the surah repeatedly depicts descent, ascent, channels, and water movement. I infer that the recipients act as passages rather than terminal stores for provision. Spending thus reads as allowing what entered from the provider to find a social outlet.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The hidden recompense in 32:17 made outward expenditure and unseen return a paired circulation. The water driven through barren ground to feed livestock and selves in 32:27 later supplied a material model for provision that must pass onward to become fruitful.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Devotion begins as a deliberate break in bodily contact.** `ج ف و:B001` is standing off from contact and explicitly includes the side separating from a bed; `ج ن ب:B001` identifies the bodily or spatial side. The present-tense verbs continue the responsive movement of 32:15 from falling in prostration to sides repeatedly drawing away from resting places. **Inferred arrow:** the bed's invitation to remain joined -> chosen separation -> wakeful calling on the Lord. The image diagnoses disciplined detachment, not mere sleeplessness.

2. **Fear and desire form a two-directional calling mechanism.** `خ و ف:B001` anticipates harm, while `ط م ع:B001` is heartfelt desire and hope. Their coordinated accusatives attach both motives to the same *yadʿūna rabbahum* without letting either replace the other. **Inferred arrow:** apprehended loss pushes away from danger + hoped-for good draws toward the Lord -> sustained invocation. The pairing keeps devotion from collapsing into either panic or appetite alone.

3. **Received provision is given an outward route.** `ر ز ق:B001` is an allotted provision or gift, and *mimmā razaqnāhum* places receipt before `ن ف ق:B002`, outward expenditure of wealth. As a secondary image, `ن ف ق:B003` is a tunnel with an exit; 32:20, still inside the focus window, will depict attempted exit from fire being blocked. **Packet relation:** gift -> expenditure is syntactically explicit. **Inferred resonance:** what arrives from the Lord is kept alive socially by finding a voluntary outlet, contrasting with the later compulsory enclosure.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 32:20 unexpectedly activated the secondary exit image of `ن ف ق:B003`. Provision voluntarily finds an outward route in 32:16, whereas those enclosed by fire repeatedly seek an exit and are returned; 32:21 adds that corrective moral return is available only before that enclosure.

topics.reason: The phrase {{ar:مِمَّا}} ({{tr:mimmā}}) {{ar:رَزَقْنَٰهُمْ}} ({{tr:razaqnāhum}}) precedes {{ar:يُنفِقُونَ}} ({{tr:yunfiqūna}}); attachment evidence treats the relative provision clause as the governed resource expression.

topics.headline: relative mā leaves the provision field unspecified
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the resource is not reduced to one category such as money, food, or knowledge.
topics.reason: The relative element introduces what was provided without a specified noun, and the following provision verb supplies the content.

topics.headline: written fusion mirrors semantic compression
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees one compact word carrying source, portion, and open relative content before the verb.
topics.reason: The surface fusion is real and aligns with the compact source-first syntax.

topics.headline: source phrase participates in body-voice-wealth architecture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah is not only about night prayer but about bodily, vocal, and material devotion.
topics.reason: The clause structure identifies three verbal beats: sides withdraw, they call, and they spend.

topics.headline: nasal sounds bind the source phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the provision-source phrase as cohesive before the final verb lands.
topics.reason: The phonetic observation is concrete and local to the fused phrase plus provision verb.

words.gloss_range: completed divine provision to them, left open in type and placed before ongoing human spending
words.prose: {{ar:رَزَقْنَٰهُمْ}} ({{tr:razaqnāhum}}) inserts the divine provider directly into the third-person portrait: “We” provided, and the suffix marks the believers as recipients. Its perfect aspect places allocation before the ongoing spending, while {{ar:مِمَّا}} ({{tr:mimmā}}) leaves the kind of provision open beyond one resource type. The provision is already given, not being sought, and the same suffix chain keeps the sleepers, callers, recipients, and spenders as one group. The word also links the Lord they call, {{ar:رَبَّهُمْ}} ({{tr:rabbahum}}), to the resources from which they spend, so worship and expenditure answer the same source.

topics.headline: one verb assigns divine giver and human recipients
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices both sides of provision inside one word: divine “We” as giver and the believers as recipients.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify a 1cp subject and 3mp object suffix on the provision verb.

topics.headline: completed provision grounds ongoing spending
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees spending as response to prior allocation, not as autonomous generosity.
topics.reason: The provision verb is perfect while {{ar:يُنفِقُونَ}} ({{tr:yunfiqūna}}) is imperfect, yielding prior allocation before ongoing expenditure.

topics.headline: first-person divine voice claims the provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the narration shift from describing them to divine speech claiming the resource source.
topics.reason: The 1cp subject changes the voice inside a third-person description, making the provision clause a direct divine claim.

topics.headline: open provision field is broad but locally an allocation act
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that what was provided can include more than money, while the local verb remains a concrete completed allocation.
topics.reason: The root range includes sustenance, livelihood, share, and provider titles; the local surface is a Form I perfect verb, not a divine name.

topics.headline: provided provision contrasts with seeking provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause is about already received provision, not acquisition or asking for resources.
topics.reason: The surface is the basic provision verb in perfect, not the Form X seeking-provision form.

topics.headline: relative provision clause mediates source and expenditure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the provision clause as the bridge between what comes from God and what leaves through the believers.
topics.reason: The verb sits inside {{ar:مِمَّا}} ({{tr:mimmā}}) before {{ar:يُنفِقُونَ}} ({{tr:yunfiqūna}}), making provided resources the source frame for spending.

topics.headline: Lordship becomes concrete provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the Lord invoked in the prayer clause is concretized as provider in the spending clause.
topics.reason: The local movement from {{ar:رَبَّهُمْ}} ({{tr:rabbahum}}) to {{ar:رَزَقْنَٰهُمْ}} ({{tr:razaqnāhum}}) is supported by co-occurrence and same-surah Lordship patterns.

topics.headline: same believers become recipients before spenders
topics.reader_payoff: The reader follows one referent chain from sleepers to callers to provision recipients and spenders.
topics.reason: Cross-reference evidence resolves the 3mp suffix to the same believer group, carrying the profile into the material clause.

words.gloss_range: ongoing plural spending/outward expenditure from provided resources, with Form IV agency and final-word closure
words.prose: {{ar:يُنفِقُونَ}} ({{tr:yunfiqūna}}) is the ayah’s final landing: ongoing human expenditure from what was first provided. The fronted {{ar:مِمَّا}} ({{tr:mimmā}}) {{ar:رَزَقْنَٰهُمْ}} ({{tr:razaqnāhum}}) has already supplied the resource frame, so the final verb is not vague objectless spending but source-governed outflow. The provision phrase selects the positive spending branch, while hidden-exit and hypocrisy associations remain contrastive background rather than the local sense. Its Form IV agency makes the believers active channelers, not people watching wealth disappear, and the root’s passage imagery helps the body’s earlier departure from beds return as the departure of resources from possession. The final plural ending keeps the same believers audible at closure and shares cadence with the earlier calling verb.

topics.headline: pro-drop plural subject leaves action at the close
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word lands on the believers’ ongoing action while their identity remains carried in the verb ending.
topics.reason: The 3mp imperfect ending supplies the subject and keeps the same believers active at closure.

topics.headline: imperfect spending follows completed provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees spending as repeated disposition after prior divine allocation.
topics.reason: Aspect contrast between {{ar:رَزَقْنَٰهُمْ}} ({{tr:razaqnāhum}}) and {{ar:يُنفِقُونَ}} ({{tr:yunfiqūna}}) supports prior provision and ongoing human response.

topics.headline: resource frame is supplied before the verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the source before the action, so spending is framed by provision rather than by possession.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:مِمَّا}} ({{tr:mimmā}}) the prepositional complement of {{ar:يُنفِقُونَ}} ({{tr:yunfiqūna}}); the delayed verb inherits that resource frame.

topics.headline: provision phrase selects positive economic outflow
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the n-f-q family’s hidden-exit and hypocrisy associations are contrasted, not selected, while sincere outward spending is active.
topics.reason: The local provision phrase selects expenditure; hypocrisy and hidden-exit imagery survive only as contrastive background, not as the local sense.

topics.headline: Form IV makes believers cause resources to pass outward
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees spending as deliberate channeling outward, not mere loss or disappearance of wealth.
topics.reason: QAC marks the verb as Form IV, supporting agentive causative outflow from the broader passage/spending root image.

topics.headline: final word turns devotion into material outflow
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah does not close on inner emotion but on outward expenditure.
topics.reason: The clause sequence and final-word placement support body-to-voice-to-wealth progression with spending as the closure.

topics.headline: spending closes a chain from Lordship to provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees generosity as downstream from the Lord they call and the provision they received.
topics.reason: Co-occurrence evidence and the local source phrase connect Lordship, provision, and spending in one sequence.

topics.headline: departure from bed returns as departure of wealth
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a bookend: bodies depart comfort at the start, resources depart possession at the end.
topics.reason: The opening {{ar:تَتَجَافَىٰ}} ({{tr:tatajāfā}}) and closing {{ar:يُنفِقُونَ}} ({{tr:yunfiqūna}}) frame the ayah with two outward movements.

topics.headline: two imperfect plural verbs share cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears calling and spending linked by the shared plural imperfect ending.
topics.reason: The surface endings of {{ar:يَدْعُونَ}} ({{tr:yadʿūna}}) and {{ar:يُنفِقُونَ}} ({{tr:yunfiqūna}}) are parallel and support the link between vocal and material actions.
